entries.purpose: Prepare gradually for running, especially faster sessions.
tech: Walk or jog gently for several minutes, then build to an easy rhythm.
Use comfortable dynamic movements such as leg swings or marching if helpful.
Before quality work, add a few short relaxed accelerations only when ready.
entries.reg: Begin with walking and an easy jog; skip accelerations if uncomfortable.
entries.prog: You can begin your planned session without feeling rushed or strained.
entries.mistake: Do not use a warm-up to push through illness, dizziness or pain.

entries.purpose: Practice relaxed fast running mechanics without an all-out sprint.
tech: After an easy warm-up, accelerate smoothly over roughly 15–20 seconds.
Stay tall and relaxed; do not force maximum speed or reach ahead with your foot.
Walk or jog until breathing and form are comfortable before repeating.
entries.reg: Use shorter, gentler accelerations on level, unobstructed ground.
entries.prog: Your stride stays smooth without straining or changing gait.
entries.mistake: Optional skill drill, not required after every run. Avoid with pain or unusual fatigue.

entries.purpose: Coordinate an upright posture and controlled alternating knee lift.
tech: March slowly with tall posture and ribs stacked over hips.
Lift one knee comfortably while keeping the other leg stable.
Set the foot underneath you and switch sides at a steady rhythm.
entries.reg: Hold a stable support if balance is limited; reduce knee height.
entries.prog: You can alternate sides without rocking or losing balance.
entries.mistake: A skill cue, not a promise to improve running economy.

entries.purpose: Explore quiet, light foot contacts with controlled ankle movement.
tech: Begin with very small steps on a level surface.
Keep the movement low amplitude, easy and quiet; do not bounce maximally.
Stop if calves, Achilles tendon or feet become uncomfortable.
entries.reg: Replace with simple marching or relaxed walking.
entries.prog: Foot contacts are comfortable and posture remains upright.
entries.mistake: Skip during calf or Achilles symptoms; technique drills do not replace easy mileage.

entries.purpose: Transition gradually from harder running to normal activity.
tech: Reduce pace to a comfortable jog or walk.
Allow breathing to settle without forcing a strict heart-rate target.
Rehydrate and recover according to conditions and the session.
entries.reg: A comfortable walk can be sufficient.
entries.prog: Breathing has settled and you can comfortably stop.
entries.mistake: A cooldown is not treatment for chest pain, faintness or other acute symptoms.

entries.purpose: Practice loaded carrying with upright posture and grip control.
tech: Hold one manageable weight in each hand and stand tall.
Walk in a clear path with quiet, even steps; keep shoulders level.
Stop before grip or posture gives way; set weights down safely.
entries.reg: Use lighter weights or a shorter clear walking path.
entries.prog: Control both weights without leaning or rushing.
entries.mistake: Check for obstacles and avoid loads you cannot safely pick up and set down.

entries.purpose: Train controlled walking while resisting a sideways lean.
tech: Hold one manageable weight at your side and stand upright.
Walk slowly without tilting toward or away from the load.
Stop, switch hands and repeat with similar control on each side.
entries.reg: Use a lighter weight or practice standing still before walking.
entries.prog: Keep trunk upright and walk without compensating.
entries.mistake: Not simply an interchangeable replacement for a farmer carry: loading is asymmetrical.

entries.purpose: Introduce bodyweight horizontal pulling with an easier, more upright angle.
tech: Verify the bar or rings are securely anchored and stable.
Walk feet forward only as far as you can keep a straight body.
Pull under control, then lower slowly without shrugging.
entries.reg: Choose a more upright angle and shorten the range.
entries.prog: Complete controlled repetitions without arching or swinging.
entries.mistake: Do not use unstable furniture or unverified door-frame anchors.

entries.purpose: Increase demand by moving the body closer to horizontal.
tech: Use a verified stable bar or rings with enough clearance.
Keep torso and hips aligned as you draw the chest toward the handles.
Lower under control, stopping before form deteriorates.
entries.reg: Return to a more upright angle.
entries.prog: Consistent reps and stable body position at the chosen angle.
entries.mistake: An angle progression, not a substitute for an unanchored pull exercise.

entries.purpose: Build upper-body support tolerance before attempting a dip.
tech: Use sturdy parallel bars at an appropriate height.
Support body weight with straight but not aggressively locked arms.
Keep shoulders comfortable and lower with assistance when done.
entries.reg: Use feet on the ground for support if the setup permits.
entries.prog: Hold a stable supported position without shoulder discomfort.
entries.mistake: Avoid forcing shoulder depression or prolonged holds with pain.

entries.purpose: Practice a controlled dip through a comfortable shoulder range.
tech: Use a reliable assistance method and secure bars.
Bend elbows slowly while keeping the shoulder range comfortable.
Press back to support without bouncing or forcing deep extension.
entries.reg: Return to supported holds or reduce the movement range.
entries.prog: Control a pain-free range without bouncing.
entries.mistake: Deep dips can aggravate shoulders; stop at discomfort and do not force depth.

entries.purpose: Develop pushing strength with controlled bodyweight support.
tech: Start in stable support with the bars firmly anchored.
Lower only through a comfortable, controllable shoulder range.
Press to a stable finish without swinging.
entries.reg: Use a verified assisted dip setup or support-hold progression.
entries.prog: Repeated smooth, pain-free repetitions with stable shoulders.
entries.mistake: Dips are not suitable for everyone; pain-free depth varies.

entries.purpose: Develop shoulder loading tolerance with feet on the floor.
tech: Place hands shoulder-width apart on a firm surface.
Bring hips up while keeping a comfortable bend at the knees.
Push the floor away and hold briefly without strain.
entries.reg: Keep more weight on the feet and shorten the hold.
entries.prog: Stable shoulders, breathing and balance throughout.
entries.mistake: Do not load the neck or force the spine into an inverted shape.

entries.purpose: Practice alignment and shoulder strength with wall support.
tech: Use clear floor space and a stable wall; start conservatively.
Move into a comfortable wall-supported position without kicking wildly.
Keep hands rooted and exit under control when tired.
entries.reg: Return to a pike hold or work with qualified supervision.
entries.prog: Controlled entry, comfortable shoulder position and a safe exit.
entries.mistake: Inversions carry fall and wrist/shoulder risks; seek appropriate coaching.

entries.purpose: Build controlled shoulder weight transfer while wall-supported.
tech: Enter an already secure wall-supported handstand.
Shift a small amount of weight from hand to hand without losing alignment.
Exit before fatigue compromises balance.
entries.reg: Stay with a static wall-supported hold.
entries.prog: Stable shifts and a predictable safe exit.
entries.mistake: Not an automatic route to freestanding handstands; use a spotter when needed.

entries.purpose: Practice trunk control during slow alternating limb motion.
tech: Lie on your back and find a comfortable rib and pelvis position.
Slowly lower an opposite arm and leg only as far as trunk position stays controlled.
Return, breathe and change sides without rushing.
entries.reg: Keep feet closer to the floor or move only one limb at a time.
entries.prog: Alternate sides smoothly without discomfort or large trunk movement.
entries.mistake: Avoid forcing a painful flat-back position.

entries.purpose: Build a compact hollow-body position with shorter leverage.
tech: Lie on your back with knees comfortably bent.
Lift shoulders only as tolerated and maintain controlled breathing.
Hold briefly without neck strain, then relax.
entries.reg: Keep head supported or reduce hold time.
entries.prog: Comfortable, controlled holds without breath-holding.
entries.mistake: Stop with neck or lower-back discomfort.

entries.purpose: Increase anti-extension demand by lengthening the body lever.
tech: Start from a comfortable hollow tuck position.
Extend arms or legs gradually without losing trunk control.
Shorten the lever as soon as your back or neck feels strained.
entries.reg: Return to a tuck hold and shorter duration.
entries.prog: Consistent pain-free breathing and position control.
entries.mistake: Not equivalent to hanging leg raises or a weighted core exercise.

entries.purpose: Develop a comfortable supported hang and grip awareness.
tech: Verify the overhead bar and surrounding clearance.
Use feet for assistance if needed and maintain a comfortable shoulder position.
Release safely before grip fails.
entries.reg: Use foot support to offload body weight.
entries.prog: Comfortable hangs with controlled entry and exit.
entries.mistake: Avoid unsupported hangs if shoulder pain or instability is present.

entries.purpose: Practice small controlled shoulder movement while hanging.
tech: Start from an appropriately assisted stable hang.
Move the shoulder blades gently without bending elbows much.
Return slowly rather than swinging.
entries.reg: Practice with feet supported.
entries.prog: Smooth motion without shoulder discomfort or swinging.
entries.mistake: This is skill preparation, not a prerequisite everyone must complete.

entries.purpose: Practice supported compression and balance as a separate core-support skill.
tech: Use stable supports with clear ground below.
Lift knees only as high as you can maintain shoulder comfort.
Lower feet safely before balance or wrist position fails.
entries.reg: Keep toes on the floor, building supported holds first.
entries.prog: Short controlled holds with safe entry and exit.
entries.mistake: A different skill branch from hollow holds, not the final rung of the same exercise.
